response: Among high bleeding risk (HBR) patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), bare-metal stent (BMS) implantation is not the most recommended option. According to the Zotarolimus-Eluting Endeavor Sprint Stent in Uncertain DES Candidates (ZEUS) trial, everolimus-zotarolimus-eluting stent (E-ZES) implantation provides superior efficacy and safety compared to conventional BMS in HBR patients with stable or unstable coronary artery disease. This suggests that BMS implantation may not be the best choice for HBR patients, and alternative options like E-ZES may be more suitable. Therefore, BMS implantation is not entirely justifiable in HBR patients undergoing PCI, and other options should be considered to optimize efficacy and safety.
